title: Metering schema, pro‑rata plan upgrades, and billing reconciliation PRD
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem statement: As we expand multi-plan offerings and introduce multi-dimensional quotas (tokens, embeddings, and vector index operations), we lack a unified metering schema and deterministic pro‑rata upgrade/downgrade behavior. This leads to ambiguous charges, incorrect overage calculations, and customer support escalations.

Goal: Define a single metering schema that supports dimensional usage (tokens, embeddings, storage, indexing), deterministic billing windows, pro‑rata calculations for mid-cycle plan changes (including trial->paid), and a reconciliation process to detect and resolve accounting drift between runtime events and billing records. Produce acceptance criteria, API contract changes, rollout plan (dry-run), and QA testcases for billing system teams and legal/compliance review.

Scope (in):
- Canonical event types and fields for metering (event_id, customer_id, timestamp, resource_type, units, unit_type, plan_id, region, route_hash).
- Multi-dimensional quota enforcement semantics (how counters increment and when quota buckets reset for rolling vs calendar windows).
- Pro‑rata charge algorithm for plan upgrades/downgrades (immediate upgrades, scheduled upgrades at period boundary, trial conversions).
- Overage detection logic and configurable grace windows for soft-limited customers.
- Billing reconciliation pipeline design: delta detection between metering events and invoiced line-items, automated alerts and reconciliation runbooks.
- Developer and customer-facing API (usage query endpoints) for up-to-date consumption and projected charges.

Out-of-scope:
- Full payment provider integrations (Stripe invoicing details) beyond agreed line-item fields.
- Changes to UI styling for billing pages (only content and flows covered).
requirements: R1: Introduce canonical metering event schema and publish JSON schema + example events
R2: Implement server-side aggregation to map events to quota buckets with support for fixed-window and rolling-window semantics
R3: Define deterministic pro‑rata formulas: credit remaining time of old plan, charge difference for new plan scaled to remaining term, handle trial edge cases
R4: Add an 'estimated_charge' field in usage API that projects invoice impact given current usage and plan settings
R5: Build reconciliation job that emits daily deltas and flags discrepancies > $0.50 or >1% per-customer
R6: Provide migration/backfill strategy for historical usage (90-day backfill window) and an audit log for adjustments
R7: Expose entitlement delta hooks for downstream systems (rate limiter, quota enforcer) so changes are effective within 60s
R8: Ensure all billing-sensitive fields are logged to an HSM-backed audit store and masked in UI where required
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Metering events conform to schema — sample dataset validated against JSON schema with zero rejections for canonical fields

AC2: Pro‑rata upgrade scenario: Customer on monthly Starter ($50/mo) at day 10 upgrades to Pro ($200/mo) and is immediately billed prorated delta = (remaining term fraction) * (Pro - Starter). Automated test demonstrates exact cents-level calculation and creates an invoice line item matching the calculation
AC3: Trial->paid conversion: Trial customers converting mid-cycle receive pro‑rata credit for unused trial convert-to-paid without double-billing; Chat transcript test case created for support

AC4: Quota enforcement test: Token quota with rolling 30-day window enforces soft-limit (grace 2 days) before hard block; simulated traffic shows soft-limit alerts and no hard block until grace exceeded
AC5: Estimated charges API returns a value within 2% of actual invoice in 90% of sampled accounts during dry-run period
AC6: Reconciliation job runs daily and publishes delta report; seeded test with injected missing events shows alert generation and a reconciliation ticket is auto-created
AC7: Migration/backfill: Historical ingestion of 60 days of events completes without data loss and reconciles to within rounding tolerances (<$1 per-customer) against baseline ledger
AC8: Security: Billing fields stored with required encryption flags and audit logs show who/when adjustments occurred
AC9: Rollout safety: Feature gated with account-level opt-in; dry-run for 5% of traffic yields no customer-facing invoice differences for controlled accounts
design_decisions: DD1: Use UTC-aligned calendar windows for invoice period boundaries but support rolling aggregation for quota enforcement
DD2: Metering schema will use integer micro-units for tokens/embeddings to avoid floating point drift
DD3: Pro‑rata charges computed in billing cents using safe integer arithmetic; round-half-away-from-zero applied at line-item level
DD4: Grace period behavior is configurable per-plan and enforced by quota enforcer, not by billing system
DD5: Reconciliation tolerance thresholds set to $0.50 or 1% to avoid alert fatigue; infra will permit per-customer overrides for enterprise accounts
tradeoffs_notes: T1: Using rolling windows improves fairness for bursty customers but increases state complexity and storage — chosen due to product promise of consistent SLOs
T2: Strict immediate billing on upgrades increases revenue predictability but risks customer surprise; mitigated with clear UI and pre-upgrade estimate API
T3: Backfilling historical events beyond 90 days is expensive and only supported via manual ops request
T4: Storing micro-unit events increases telemetry volume; we'll sample high-cardinality routes for analytics to reduce cost
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Spec review and security sign-off (legal + compliance) — team: PM, Billing Eng, Security
Phase 1: Implement canonical schema + ingest pipeline; enable for internal dry-run accounts (0%)
Phase 2: Billing dry-run (5% accounts, read-only invoicing lane); monitor delta metrics for 14 days
Phase 3: Opt-in pilot (managed customers); enable pro‑rata billing for pilot accounts and collect support feedback
Phase 4: Gradual ramp to 50% with feature flag and 24/7 on-call coverage
Phase 5: Full rollout and deprecation of legacy heuristics; 30-day post-rollout reconciliation audit
monitoring_and_metrics: SLO: reconciliation job completes within 2 hours daily
qa_testcases: TC1: End-to-end scenario: Upgrade/downgrade mid-cycle using test account, assert invoice line items and account balance
TC2: Inject missing meter events: run reconciliation, assert alert and corrective ticket creation
TC3: High-throughput simulation: 50k events/min real-time ingest; verify no more than 5% event processing lag
TC4: Edge rounding test: Verify cent rounding behavior across 100k randomized pro‑rata calculations
TC5: Security test: Audit log immutability and masking verification
implementation_notes: Infra: Add kafka topic 'metering.canonical' with 7-day retention and schema registry
Billing Eng: Provide a 'dry_run=true' mode on invoice generator to create but not charge line items
Runtime: Quota enforcer must fetch entitlement changes within 60s using subscription webhook or push protocol
Data: Backfill worker to process 90-day window and mark processed ranges with checkpointing
Docs: Publish API contract + examples in DevDocs and update Console pricing flow text
